name: npc_cc-mamoru
customDialogue:
Mamoru lifts her skull candle. Her emerald eyes gleam beneath the bones of her suit.
The Harvest Moon called me home. Where the Coven gathers, I keep the watch.
Tricksters slip in from beyond the veil on harvest nights. My candle sends them home.

name: npc_cc-flower-moon
customDialogue:
Kokeshi Flower Moon hums a melody as soft as a nightingale's song.
When the Flower Moon takes its throne, the sleeping buds wake and the whole hill breathes out in colour.
Be grateful for what is beautiful, be patient, and tend your seeds. Every ending here is a beginning.

name: npc_cc-mochi
customDialogue:
Mochi lifts his right paw and beckons. Luck in, luck in!
I am Mochi. So long as I am near, no darkness shall harm you.
The game hall never closes. Win or lose, nobody here walks alone.

name: npc_cc-ostara
customDialogue:
Ostara sits still as starlight, her head tilted to the moon. A tiny silver bell chimes at her neck.
They call me the Dreamer. I watch the moon, and the moon watches over everything that grows.
Listen. Can you hear the sap rising in the trees?

name: npc_cc-nariko
customDialogue:
Lightning crackles in the orb between her hands.
The graves here are restless when the storm comes. I keep them sleeping.
Stay close to the candles and the spirits will leave you be.

hotspots.description: The Mystic Moon Coven, painted by moonlight, each under their own moon: Mamoru with her skull candle, Mochi with his beckoning paw, Kokeshi Flower Moon, Ostara the Dreamer, and Nariko over the door. Their portraits watch the door so nobody comes in uninvited.
It has burned purple since the night the manor was built. Nobody remembers putting wood on it.
The great coffin has no handles, only a keyhole that glows when someone with the right key comes near.
Every skull has a name and a little bow. The crypt keeper dusts them every full moon and tells each one the news.

Something green and friendly is bubbling. Her note is pinned to the beam above it, in silver ink: "One for each moon. A cherry petal for the Pink, a sleepy bud for the Flower, a silver chime for the Hare, a crumb of moon cake for the Harvest. Stir until it tastes like friendship." The Lunar Witch says it is soup. The bats say otherwise.
Half the pages are spells, half are recipes, and the Lunar Witch is not always sure which is which.
The Lunar Witch's recipe page lies open by the cauldron: a riddle for each ingredient. Pour them in order.
Roll a six and the ghosts cheer; roll a one and they follow you home for a night.
The crystal ball only ever shows good fortunes. The bad ones it keeps to itself.
Every plushie in it is a member of the gang. Win one and it is yours to keep, and it will keep you company.
Pumpkins for balls, bones for pins. Strike all ten and the pins clap.

spotConfig.label: Read the grave
spotConfig.text: A plain stone on a fresh mound. No name, no date, only a small 13 scratched at the bottom. The earth under your feet is warm, and something behind the stone goes click.

spotConfig.label: Stir the cauldron
spotConfig.text: Round and round. The green brew goes purple, then gold, and a bubble the size of a pumpkin floats up and pops: it smells of toffee apples. The Lunar Witch would be proud.

spotConfig.label: Follow the ghost
spotConfig.startText: The ghost giggles and drifts off. Stay close!
spotConfig.failText: The ghost slipped away into the fog. Try again from where it started.
spotConfig.text: All the way round, and you never lost it. The ghost stops, turns, and does a tiny bow before it fades into the fog.

spotConfig.label: Look up at the turret
spotConfig.text: High in the west turret a candle moves from window to window, top to bottom, as if someone were coming down the stairs to meet you. Then it goes out.

spotConfig.label: Count the skeleton
spotConfig.text: One.

requires.hint: The great tree is waiting for its lanterns. Come back after dark.

spotConfig.text: Under the great tree every lantern is lit, and their light runs down the bark into the roots. For a moment the whole tree glows from the inside, like a heart.

spotConfig.label: Look inside the pumpkin
spotConfig.text: Inside the biggest pumpkin, curled up on the seeds, a tiny ant is asleep. It opens one eye and whispers something.

spotConfig.label: Read the welcome sign
spotConfig.text: WELCOME TO CUTE & CREEPY. Wipe your feet, mind the ghosts, and please do not wake the scarecrows. Underneath, in small neat letters: Rebels welcome. Biting optional. The Mystic Moons.

spotConfig.label: Watch the moon rise
spotConfig.text: The Harvest Super Moon swells full, huge, golden and fat over the manor roofs. Its light pours down the hill and chases the shadows out of even the darkest corners.

spotConfig.text: Thirty breaths under the old tree. Your heart feels lighter, the way the hill does after rain.

spotConfig.failText: The chime fades. Go back to the library and listen again.
spotConfig.text: The last shimmer settles on a stone ledge behind the manor, one nobody ever seems to notice.

spotConfig.label: Gaze at the moon

spotConfig.text: Over the hill the sky turns pale gold: the first blush of dawn.

riddle.title: The First Grave
riddle.solvedText: The well. Its moon is still down there.

parts.text: Here lies one who was full of stars at night and full of buckets by day. Lean over me and the moon looks back up at you. Where did I go?

riddleAnswer.text: The old well. Somewhere far below, the moon winks.

riddle.title: The Second Grave
riddle.solvedText: The scarecrows. They still keep the crows guessing.

parts.text: Here lies one who stood in the field all night without any feet. The crows thought I was the farmer; the farmer knew I was straw. Find my brothers.

riddleAnswer.text: The scarecrow field. Twelve straw brothers, and not one of them blinks.

riddle.title: The Third Grave
riddle.solvedText: The witch's cauldron. It bubbles on without its ghost.

parts.text: Here lies one who bubbled green every night and never once boiled over. The witch stirred me, but I never went round. Find my pot.

riddleAnswer.text: The witch's cauldron. A green bubble pops: thank you.
The crypt door is cold to the touch. Chalked across it: go back to where the map was given.
Plenty of guests here, and every one of them leaves by morning. Look for a house that nobody lives in.

riddles.q: What has a head and a tail, but no body?
riddles.why: Mochi keeps a pawful of them for luck.

riddles.q: I am lighter than a feather, yet the strongest ant cannot hold me for five minutes. What am I?
Three jars are labelled Candy, Bones and Mixed, and every label is wrong. You may take one thing from one jar without looking in. Which jar do you pick from to fix all three labels?
riddles.why: The jar labelled Mixed is not mixed, so one piece tells you what it really holds. The other two labels can then only swap one way.

riddles.q: What gets wetter the more it dries?
riddles.why: The witch’s towel after a long night of brewing.

riddles.q: Some months have 30 days, some 31. How many have 28?
riddles.why: Every month has at least 28 days.
